content:
For years, collectors have had a fascination with Steve Jobs memorabilia, and a new item is poised to generate significant interest. It's an eighth-grade science fair project featuring two demonstration circuits — along with a warning note Jobs left for his teacher.

It has been kept at the Jobs family property in Los Altos, but is now one of over 200 lots in the Apple 50th anniversary auction...

Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and RR Auctions is holding a two-part sale called "Steve Jobs and the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction." In the first part, the company's first-ever check sold for a staggering $2.4 million.

The second part includes this science fair project.

The warning note likely reflects one risk: the circuits could burn out if left running too long. At the time of writing, online bidding remained under $3,000, but we expect that number will certainly change.

The auction also includes a fully functional early Apple 1.

As well as a development prototype of the original iPod.
